method: The ladder follows the widely used strength-training ramp: five reps with the empty bar, then five reps at 40 percent, three at 60 percent, two at 80 percent and one at 90 percent of the working weight, with percentages taken from the total working weight including the bar. A bar can only reach its own weight plus a whole number of times twice the smallest plate pair, because plates load in pairs, so every rung is rounded onto that grid: loadable = bar + 2 x pair x round((ideal - bar) / (2 x pair)), with half-step ties rounded up and anything at or below the bar pinned to the bar. A rung that rounds onto a load already in the ladder is dropped and counted, which is why a very light working weight shows only the bar and the heaviest rung that fits above it. The working weight itself is rounded onto the same grid and the difference is reported, so 101 kg entered against 1.25 kg pairs is shown as 100 kg. Reps and percentages are a coaching convention rather than a computed optimum: the tool does not know the lifter's training history, does not model fatigue, technique, injury or recovery, and is not medical, physiotherapy or rehabilitation advice. Inputs are bounded to 1000 of the chosen unit of working weight, a 100 bar ceiling, and pairs from 0.25 to 20, accept at most two decimal places, and reject exponent notation instead of silently parsing it. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: StrongLifts 5x5 warm-up protocol: two sets of five with the empty bar, then five reps at 40 percent, three at 60 percent, two at 80 percent and one at 90 percent of the working weight.
Starting Strength (Rippetoe) warm-up guidance: ramp sets expressed as percentages of the work-set weight with reps decreasing as the load rises.
International Powerlifting Federation, Technical Rules Book: 20 kg and 15 kg bars loaded with 25, 20, 15, 10, 5, 2.5 and 1.25 kg discs, loaded in matching pairs.
Standard Olympic weight sets in pounds: a 45 lb bar with 45, 35, 25, 10, 5 and 2.5 lb plates, so the smallest available pair sets the loadable step.

Plates are loaded symmetrically, so every additional kilogram on the bar is twice the per-side pair; that symmetry is why the ladder is quantised to two times the smallest pair rather than to the pair itself.
